CFItems.fullStatement: Major elements of emergent literacy theory and major conclusions of recent research
Factors influencing the development of emergent reading
social interaction (support by adults and peers)
Address the role of comprehension in reading development.

comprehension as a strategic process
* solving words
* adjusting reading according to purpose and context
* metacognition
* maintaining fluency
* making connections (personal, world, text)
* drawing inferences and conclusions
Understand the basic elements of literature and informational texts.
evaluate the clarity of the information
identify the author’s point of view or perspective
make valid inferences or conclusions based on the selection

plot elements
* rising action
* internal and external conflict complication
* suspense crisis
* climax or turning point
characterization (through a character’s words, thoughts, actions, appearance, etc.)
setting (established through description of scenes, colors, smells, etc.)
point of view (first person, third person objective, third-person omniscient)
perspective (attitude of the narrator of the story)
identify, where appropriate, an author’s appeal to reason, appeal to emotion, or appeal to authority
Evaluate the relationship between stated generalizations and actual evidence given
Evaluate the organization of a selection
For informational texts, evaluate the effectiveness of their organizational and graphic aids
Address the basic elements of poetry (e.g., verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., puppetry, story theatre).

verse
* meter 
* stanza
* line length 
* punctuation

rhyme and sound 
* patterns 
* rhyme scheme 
* onomatopoeia
* repetition of words 
* alliteration 
* assonance

imagery and figures of speech 
* image
* personification 
* metaphor 
* simile 
* hyperbole

poetic types and forms
* lyrical
* concrete
* free verse
* narrative
* couplet
* elegy
* sonnet
* limerick
* haiku

construction of meaning in poetry
* main idea or theme
* symbolism
* tone, emotion
Understand how to determine the meanings of words and phrases as used in texts, including figurative language. Be ready to define these terms and/or identify examples of them.
Address the components of written language (e.g., elements of grammar, usage, syntax).

phrase
* participial phrase
* prepositional phrase
* appositive phrase
verb tenses: present, past, present perfect, past perfect, future, and future perfect
voice of verb: active or passive
correct use of infinitive and participle
Address sentence types (e.g., declarative, imperative) and sentence structures (e.g., simple, compound, complex).
Address the basic components of vocabulary (e.g., affixes, root words, context clues).
Cues and how students use them
Address types (e.g., narrative, persuasive, journaling) and traits (e.g., tone, purpose, audience) of writing.
Address the stages of the writing process (e.g., draft, edit, publish).
Address structures (e.g., description, definition, examples) and organization (e.g., descriptive, comparison/contrast, persuasive) of writing.
Address how to use resource material (e.g., types of resources, graphic organizers) in reading and language arts.
primary sources, including reproductions of original documents
appropriateness of various sources to the project
Focus, organization, structure, point of view
Understand different aspects of listening (e.g., following directions, responding to questions appropriately, focusing on the speaker).
Agreeing or disagreeing with the ideas in a speech
Repeating or paraphrasing to verify one’s understanding
Summarizing major ideas and supporting evidence
Understand different aspects of viewing (e.g., interpreting images, evaluating media techniques, understanding the message).
Understand the role that speaking, listening, and viewing play in language acquisition for second-language learners.
